q1_issues.issue: The restrictor "in the world" is dropped entirely — no atom records the domain over which the superlative ranks.
(Inheritance woman thing) is taxonomic (no counterexample conceivable), so the confidence dial calls for 0.99, not the empirical 0.9.

q2_gaps: superlative with a stated comparison domain ("the ADJ-est N in/of <domain>") — (Most <scale> X <class>) has no slot for the restrictor, and the instruction set only covers the bare-noun and no-noun cases
superlative predicated of a generic kind subject rather than an individual — the Most examples all take an individual in the X slot, and the companion class atom is shown only as Member
notes: Scale lemmatization (sweetest to sweet) and argument order in (Most sweet woman thing) follow the superlative rule, and reading indefinite "a woman" as the generic kind in a copular predication is the licensed route. The figurative/hyperbolic force of the sentence is taken literally, which the instruction set gives no other option for.
